attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter post, stated as his own assertion.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his exact phrase. It is a causal claim that the deployment harmed and killed people. It is not hedged and has no conditions.

contract.note: Including Autopilot is an ordinary reading. Tesla labelled Autosteer as beta (e1), and Zitron named no narrower product. Accepting a contributing cause and a cumulative period up to the post date fits the present-perfect wording. Reading it narrowly as FSD Beta would leave the claim unresolved, so the interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: NTSB report on the 2018 Mountain View crash, published 2020. One driver died and another was injured. NTSB found Autopilot steering and weak driver monitoring causal or contributing, and the report documents the beta designation.

NTSB report on the 2019 Delray Beach crash, published 2020. The driver died with Autopilot engaged. NTSB found Tesla's system design and its failure to restrict use to intended conditions contributed.
News report of a 2023 jury verdict clearing Tesla in a separate injury case. A finding on one unrelated crash does not negate the NTSB findings or the cumulative claim.

reviews.rationale: Two completed NTSB investigations, both published before September 2023, found that Tesla's Autopilot behaviour or safeguards contributed to public-road crashes that killed two drivers and injured another. That meets the contract's support condition. The Hsu verdict covers a separate crash and does not contradict this. Proof about FSD Beta specifically is not needed under the plain reading.
